title: code/* branch pipelines run the gate jobs without a click
goal: In .gitlab-ci.yml the jobs the ci-code-branch gate of ST-vcf3r6qv “sync --push sends code-lane work as a merge request” names run without a click in pipelines of code/* branches (a first rule on $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH =~ /^code\//), and every other job and branch keeps its rules; TestCiCodeBranch in _tools/test_ci_config.py reads the file as text and asserts it; git.md says what runs where

gates.question: kb-tests and kb-trailers already start on their own in every branch pipeline, code/* included, but with allow_failure: true, so a failed test leaves the pipeline successful and auto-merge would merge the code/<id> merge request untested. How do they fail on code/* branches?
options: allow_failure: false on code/* branches only: a failed gate job fails the branch pipeline and auto-merge waits; main and other branches keep allow_failure: true
keep allow_failure: true everywhere: auto-merge merges whatever the tests say
allow_failure: false on every branch, main included
gates.recommendation: allow_failure: false on code/* branches only: a failed gate job fails the branch pipeline and auto-merge waits; main and other branches keep allow_failure: true
gates.answer: superseded by the all-manual CI decision (b8c95fc): every job is manual and merge requests merge on a skipped pipeline; the code/* rules are gone, no task

notes: The test reads the YAML as text: no new dependency. kb-trailers' rule ($CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "push" && $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH) matches a code/* push. .github/workflows/kb.yml runs every job on every pushed branch already, so it needs no change.
